requirement: Merged hit set equals defined union on identical source

inputs.name: default
inputs.call: check.py -> real gd-tools coverage merge on two hand-crafted, disjoint coverage-data files against the same plan (gd-tools-cli 0.4.0)

measured_with_gd_tools_0_4_0.plan_lines: line 4 (if-header, branch id 1), line 5 (true-branch body, id 0), line 6 (false-branch body, id 2)
measured_with_gd_tools_0_4_0.finding: Merging two complementary runs (each touching a disjoint subset of the file's tracked lines/branches) produces exactly the union of what each run touched, with each line's own count preserved unchanged -- no line either run covered is lost, and no line neither run covered is invented.

notes: Uses hand-crafted coverage-data JSON (same technique as F071) rather than two real GUT test runs, so the input hit counts are exact and independently known, not derived from timing-sensitive real execution -- the real gd-tools plan_generator.generate_plan() is still used to obtain the actual line-id assignments for real subject.gd, so the fixture's ground truth is anchored to genuine tool behavior, not invented ids. Confirmed the real `gd-tools coverage merge` CLI (not a reimplementation) against real gd-tools-cli 0.4.0. Since gd-tools' merge policy is arithmetic summation per (file_id, line_id) (established in F071's finding: 5+7=12, 3+2=5), a complementary pair where each line is touched by only one run is the simplest case where summation and set-union coincide (each line's final count equals whichever single run touched it, since the other run contributes 0 by omission) -- this fixture confirms that coincidence holds, not that gd-tools performs a logical union distinct from summation.

ambiguities: Does not test a genuinely overlapping merge (both runs touching the SAME line) with different counts -- that is exactly F071's already-established finding (counts sum, e.g. 5+7=12), included here only by cross-reference, not re-verified in this fixture.
